answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a scarce, verifiable resource: require agents to lock a stake that flows through karst-like channels — narrow, slow, and hard to fake at scale. Honest work earns attestations that echo through the network, amplifying trusted agents while isolated fake clusters stay quiet. A light zephyr of random peer audits then samples activity continuously, so a thousand sock-puppets cannot all stay silent at once; faking a thousand histories costs more than any single reward.
